routing_warnings.description: The request to make the spout more closely match the diagram and preserve froth primarily changes the spout configuration rather than the BOM artifact.
The observed plumbing leak is runtime failure evidence for the leak-free plumbing Requirement rather than proof that the demonstration artifact was completed.
The completed plumbing-repair claim belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement; the message only states an intention to make a demonstration video.
The cracked fitting identifies the cause of the plumbing failure and belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement.
The no-leaks statement is an implementation claim for leak-free plumbing, while recording the final demonstration remains a future intention.
The concrete runtime failure is a plumbing leak rather than a failure of dual-station operation.
The completed repair claim specifically concerns the plumbing leak.
The concern about retaining frothiness after liquid passes through the spout concerns the dispensing path rather than whisk-driven mixing performance.
The concrete runtime failure is a plumbing leak, not a demonstrated failure of splash containment during mixing.
This message requests a future demonstration and reports no observed splash-control outcome.
The request for bowls that can be removed and swapped quickly concerns bowl removability rather than bowl size or geometry.
The request to show several minutes of continuous operation defines demonstration content and does not clearly change the existing durability requirement.
This message requests a final uninterrupted liquid test; it does not report a completed continuous-operation result for the target Requirement.
The concrete observed outcome is a plumbing leak; the broad statement that all functions operated as expected does not specifically verify controlled dispensing.
The completed repair claim concerns the plumbing leak rather than the controlled-dispensing behavior.
The cracked fitting identifies the cause of the plumbing leak and does not establish a controlled-dispensing transition.
The no-leaks claim concerns plumbing integrity; the generic statement about everything operating does not specifically verify button actuation or controlled flow.
The observed plumbing leak establishes failure of plumbing integrity but does not report liquid reaching the base or electrical components.
The completed plumbing repair is a target-specific implementation claim for leak-free plumbing, not electrical isolation.
The claim that the repaired plumbing has no leaks concerns plumbing integrity and does not verify separation from electrical components.
The requested beige shade is a visual color-scheme decision rather than a change to the platform's cup-clearance mechanism.
The possible change to the logo and text on the base belongs to the independently defined base-branding Requirement.
The instruction to reproduce the rendering aesthetically for the machine and separate base concerns visual styling rather than the platform's clearance behavior.
The upgrade to a 50A AC/DC adapter and higher-power controllers addresses system load capacity and overheating rather than changing the selected 120V wall-power source.
The client's preference for the rendering-style power button concerns decorative control styling rather than master on/off behavior.
The requested light surrounding the power button concerns accent lighting rather than master power-control behavior.
The request that the buttons be functional concerns their dispensing behavior rather than control-panel placement.
Adding the on/off slot is a target-specific implementation claim for the master power control rather than the overall panel layout.
The requested silver DJ-style buttons and knobs concern decorative control styling rather than physical control-panel usability.
Recreating the rendered buttons and deck labels is a visual-styling change rather than a control-panel layout change.
The same message reports a plumbing leak, which is failure evidence for the leak-free plumbing Requirement rather than structural stability.
The beige K treatment on green dispense buttons belongs to the narrower dispense-button marking Requirement.
The accepted instruction concerns the placard behind the motor towers, not branding on the separate support base.
The requested light surrounding the power button concerns the separate power-button accent-lighting Requirement rather than bowl accent lighting.
The proposed replacement of the current on/off switch with a render-style button concerns the physical master power control rather than specifically requiring accent lighting.
The client's LED acceptance resolves the immediately preceding proposal for lights surrounding the bowls, while the separate power-button replacement proposal remains unclear.
The potential lighting discussed here is lighting for the base and does not specifically entail power-button accent lighting.
The clause requesting measurement units around the bowls belongs to the separate bowl-markings Requirement.
The requested lights are independently represented by the bowl accent-lighting Requirement.
The request for measuring units around the bowls belongs to the separate bowl-markings Requirement.
The proposed K treatment belongs to the separate dispense-button marking Requirement.
The freelancer's proposal to add measuring units concerns the separate bowl-markings Requirement.
The proposed K markings concern the separate dispense-button marking Requirement.
The lighting proposal concerns the separate accent-lighting Requirement.
The bottom-logo clause belongs to the separate support-base branding Requirement.
The Deck 1 and Deck 2 labels belong to the separate deck-label Requirement.
The light surrounding the power button belongs to the separate power-button accent-lighting Requirement.
The back-panel design and font belong to the separate back-panel styling Requirement.
The client explicitly keeps the K button markings in the current prototype rather than deferring them with the broader cosmetic redesign.
The client leaves possible lighting under discussion, so its lifecycle should be assessed separately from the deferred DJ-control redesign.
